rule: Additive register. No historical artefact is edited, banner-ed, struck through or rewritten. Each row records a claim AS PUBLISHED plus the correction a reader should use; the correction never edits the original. Where a defensible number exists it is copied from a cited grade JSON, never computed here.

error_classes.checked: Claim is over a defensible denominator (usually checkpoint / decidable cells n=3), or the denominator is stated and is the right population for the instrument (e.g. 190-case MCQ, 73-row locator audit).
error_classes.wrong_denominator: Proportion over the wrong population: the row population printed as if it were checkpoint accuracy.
error_classes.undetermined: Accuracy-shaped number published with no denominator stated anywhere on the line, and none recoverable from a cited source.

definitions.checkpoint: grade_v5 checkpoint cells; decidable = pass + fail; n is the decidable checkpoint count (3 in the current fixture).
definitions.row: rows of the run transcript (64 or 72 here) - a population of turns, not of graded checkpoints.
definitions.turn: turns in a schedule; only an accuracy denominator if the grader grades per turn, which it does not.

worst.why: It is the first-published live cell of a flagship arm, it prints a ratio whose numerator and denominator both look like a graded count, it attaches a wilson95 interval [0.7538, 0.9242] that no reader can distinguish from a real interval, and it says '(undecidable: 0)' - three separate signals of measurement that all belong to a row population. Prominence (a cell transcript is what an operator quotes) times wrongness (0.8594 published against a true checkpoint accuracy of 1.0000) makes it the most damaging line in the family.
worst.replacement_sentence: accuracy 3/3 (denominator=checkpoint, n=3 decidable, decidable=3; interval withheld - n=3 is below the reported-precision floor), source cell-transcript-grow-20261026T144452Z.grade-v5.json:arms.transcript-grow.checkpoint_accuracy; the 55/64 row-level ratio in the analyser's raw output is not accuracy.

guard_recommendation.single_change: Make the producer stamp the denominator kind and n on every accuracy line, and make a linter fail any published accuracy line that omits it.
guard_recommendation.why_this_file: analyze_stats.py is the only code that emits these lines (both the .md and the .json carry its captured output), so one emit-side change covers every future artefact; the test file is where the repo's other artefact guards already live and is collected by the same runner.

next_unit_hint: Nothing in history needs editing per this card's rule, but two things should be decided by a fresh unit: (1) cell-transcript-grow-20261026T144{452,540}Z.{md,json} keep a machine-readable "accuracy": "55/64" field that any script can consume - whether to add a sibling "accuracy_checkpoint": "3/3" + "accuracy_denominator": "row" field (additive, history untouched) is a policy call; (2) docs/DECIDABILITY-SEAM.md:57-60 references the v6 live cell's refusal, which this register supersedes with the 1/3 checkpoint number from that run's grade JSON - a correction note there, not a rewrite, would close the seam.
